CODE
Art. 2.3.59. 
Invalidity in the event of unworthiness 
Any clause in the matrimonial agreement granting an advantage which would result for the surviving spouse from the method of composition, operation, liquidation or division of the joint estate is invalid if that spouse is unworthy of inheriting from the deceased spouse.
The provisions relating to unworthiness to inherit apply by analogy to unworthiness to receive or retain benefits that would result for the surviving spouse from the method of composition, operation, liquidation or division of the joint patrimony. This is the case even if the surviving spouse is excluded from the deceased spouse's succession, either by the effect of a clause excluding him or her from the succession, or by the effect of a decision excluding or forfeiting his or her succession rights.
